documents: McCrackin et al. 2022, 3D resistivity survey over mapped caves in eogenetic karst terrane, west-central Florida, USA, Journal of Cave and Karst Studies 84(1):1-13 (published PDF)

entry.evidence: This study assesses the capability and practical applications of quasi-3 Dimensional (3D) Electrical Resistivity Tomography (ERT) for mapping air-filled conduits in eogenetic karst.

steps.action: Cite the expectation that high primary porosity and sediment infilling in eogenetic karst reduce the resistivity contrast between caves and host rock, making voids harder to detect than in telogenetic karst.
steps.quote: act to reduce the resistivity contrast between caves and rock

steps.action: Pose the question of how well quasi-3D ERT survey and modelling strategies detect voids in shallow eogenetic karst, where the method has not been described.
steps.quote: have not, to our knowledge, been described in shallow, thinly mantled eogenetic karst terranes

steps.action: Select a field site on the Brooksville Ridge that overlies two well-documented air-filled vadose caves (Legend and Bottlecap), so that resistivity images can be checked against known targets.
steps.quote: The site was selected because it overlies two well-documented vadose caves

steps.action: Set out the rival acquisition and processing strategies to compare: Dipole-Dipole, Inverse Schlumberger and combined arrays; profile orientation; L1 versus L2 inversion; Wenner is excluded a priori.
steps.quote: we consider the relative value of Dipole-Dipole and Inverse Schlumberger measurements and their combination

steps.action: Cite literature expectations that L1 (robust) inversion is more accurate for abrupt boundaries and noisy data, and L2 is more common but blurs boundaries.
steps.quote: has been described as the more accurate of the two methods

steps.action: Survey both caves to UIS grade 5, reduce the data in COMPASS, georeference the caves in ArcGIS, and build simplified 3D cave models (about 0.5 to 1 m accuracy) as ground truth.
steps.quote: Each of the caves in this study area was mapped to the Union Internationale de Spéléogie UIS

steps.action: Use a 2D synthetic forward model to choose the transect layout: 56 electrodes at 2 m spacing, 110 m lines and 4 m line spacing, with the layout constrained by site access.
steps.quote: A 2D synthetic model was created to determine the optimum transect layout prior to surveying

steps.action: Acquire 31 ERT transects (22 E-W, plus orthogonal lines over each cave) with both Dipole-Dipole and Inverse Schlumberger data, together with LiDAR topography for terrain correction.
steps.quote: On each profile, both the Dipole-Dipole and Inverse Schlumberger data sets were acquired.

steps.action: Invert the data in EarthImager: remove outliers above 40% misfit, apply terrain correction, run 2D inversions and 3D block inversions of up to six profiles (limited by memory), and vary the inversion parameters.
steps.quote: in batches of up to six adjacent profiles

steps.action: Compare 2D inversions of Transect 29 for each array geometry against the mapped Legend Cave; Dipole-Dipole and merged arrays show a stronger contrast at the cave top, and none images the cave base.
steps.quote: None of the 2D arrays properly captures information about the base of the cave

steps.action: Compare 2D and 3D inversions over Legend Cave; 3D better recovers the cave bottom and overall structure, while 2D better fits the cave top.
steps.quote: the 3D inversion better recovers the bottom and general structure of Legend Cave

steps.action: Check profiles that do not cross a mapped cave; an isolated 2D anomaly on T2 disappears in the 3D inversion of T1-T3, indicating an off-line artifact in 2D.
steps.quote: indicates an apparent anomaly that is absent in a 3D inversion

steps.action: Compare L1 and L2 3D inversions over Legend Cave; L2 better reproduces the known cave and is adopted, contrary to earlier reports.
steps.quote: the L2-norm smooth inversion was determined to be the method that better reproduced known features

steps.action: Compare 3D blocks from cave-oblique (E-W) and cave-parallel (NE-SW) profiles over Bottlecap Cave; neither matches the mapped passage, so the result is inconclusive.
steps.quote: The results are inconclusive, as neither dataset showed agreement with the mapped cave passage location.

steps.action: Compare resistivities at cross-over points of perpendicular transects; discrepancies of 50 to 8,000 ohm-m show large uncertainty in the 2D-derived values.
steps.quote: These cross-over errors range from 50 Ωm to 8,000 Ωm

steps.action: Compare the seven terrain-corrected 3D Dipole-Dipole smooth block models with both caves; there is general correspondence in location and depth, but significant mismatches in void shape.
steps.quote: the seven 3D Dipole-Dipole Models showed some correlations between resistivity highs and the sites of the two known cave systems

steps.action: Propose that other cave-like resistivity highs, especially north of Legend Cave, are unmapped voids, citing the nearby Dames Caves complex and the literature on Brooksville Ridge voids; this is not tested.
steps.quote: The resistivity data suggest that significant unmapped void features may

steps.action: Compile a 3D site model in Voxler and choose iso-surface thresholds from cross-over plots (375 ohm-m for Legend, 2,000 ohm-m for Bottlecap); the iso-surfaces resolve the mapped structures poorly.
steps.quote: the 375 Ωm contour conforms most closely to the known Legend Cave location

steps.action: Overlay the 3D cave meshes on resistivity iso-surfaces in Paraview and Maya; the large rooms merge into one anomaly and the tight passages are not detected.
steps.quote: in other cases very tight passages were not detected at all

steps.action: Offer two rival explanations for the higher resistivity on E-W lines than on N-S lines: resistivity anisotropy, or different soil moisture during acquisition.
steps.quote: This could be indicative of an overall anisotropy in the resistivity, or of data sets acquired under different soil moisture conditions.

steps.action: Argue against both: the caves are not parallel, so void orientation does not imply anisotropy, and no different rainfall conditions were noted; the discrepancy is left unexplained.
steps.quote: Significantly different rainfall conditions were not noted

steps.action: Keep the claim that quasi-3D ERT with Dipole-Dipole arrays and L2 inversion improves on 2D profiles in eogenetic karst, but loses resolution with depth and misses smaller cavities.
steps.quote: quasi-3D ERT for mapping air-filled caves in the vadose zone of eogenetic karst in west-central Florida is an improvement over simple 2D profiles

tree.answer: Detectability of known air-filled caves by quasi-3D ERT in eogenetic karst
Caves observed directly by cave survey; subsurface resistivity only inferred by inversion
Assess survey and inversion strategies of quasi-3D ERT
Rival strategies: array type, 2D vs 3D, L1 vs L2, profile orientation; for the E-W/N-S offset, anisotropy vs soil moisture
Cited expectations (3D better; L1 better for abrupt boundaries) give distinct predictions against mapped caves
Conditions found: site chosen over two mapped caves; acquisition design fixed by synthetic model and site access
Partly: a 2D artifact is removed by 3D; cross-over errors are large; the orientation test is inconclusive
3D better than 2D, Dipole-Dipole with L2 best here; small and deep conduits not resolved

end.claim: Quasi-3D ERT gives generally better agreement with mapped caves than isolated 2D lines in eogenetic karst, with good near-surface resolution of large cavities but diminished resolution with depth and inability to detect smaller cavities.

decisive_move.sentence: Comparing the 2D and 3D inversion results against the independently surveyed cave geometries is what allows any statement about the method's performance.

gates.evidence: Acquisition was designed to compare stated strategies (arrays, inversion norms, orientation), with the layout set by a synthetic model before surveying (p. 6), but no hypothesis about the result directed the data collection. Each strategy was scored against mapped caves and could fail; the orientation test did fail (inconclusive, p. 8) and L2 beat the expected L1 (p. 7). The layout and the 40% misfit cutoff were fixed before inversion; evaluation criteria were subjective ('subjectively better fits', p. 7) and iso-surface thresholds were tuned to the known caves (p. 9).

limits: The process record is thin. The synthetic forward-model results used to design the survey are not shown (p. 6). Comparisons between strategies are visual and qualitative ('subjectively better fits', p. 7); no misfit metric between resistivity and cave geometry is reported. The tested inversion parameter combinations are not listed and their results are not reported beyond the chosen settings (p. 6). The 3D inversions were split into blocks of up to six profiles because of memory limits, so full-volume behaviour is untested (p. 6). Iso-surface thresholds were tuned to the known caves, so their agreement with the caves is not an independent test (p. 9). The unmapped-void interpretation is a hypothesis with no drilling or other check (pp. 8-10). The E-W/N-S resistivity offset stays unexplained after both rivals are argued against (p. 10). Only two caves at one site were tested, so generalization to other eogenetic karst is not shown. Inference: the conclusion that a synthetic model was 'highly beneficial for selecting the most appropriate array geometry' (p. 10) is not backed by reported synthetic results. Composition is none_fits: the walk is a benchmark of an existing method against known ground-truth targets at one site; it neither builds a new capability nor establishes a phenomenon, and it is not strong inference among hypotheses.

disagreements.quote: This is contrary to the results of other cave studies.
